decisions.reason: As a bread close to the traditional core range, it likely uses existing skills and ingredients, and if it is still sold in 2022 management would tend to continue it rather than admit a failed launch with only limited evidence of poor performance.
This sweet pastry fits the established bakery business, so despite modest sunk costs the firm would usually keep such a familiar extension unless weak sales had become unmistakable.

The farmhouse bread is a highly compatible product for a heritage bakery, and escalation of commitment supports retention because discontinuing a core-style launch would offer little gain and signal an avoidable mistake.

The poppy seed Christmas stollen received visible separate promotion and a gold award, which raises public commitment and makes management especially likely to preserve it as part of the firm's festive identity.

The premium Christmas stollen is also award-backed and closely tied to the firm's traditional seasonal specialties, so management is likely to continue it unless there is very clear evidence that demand has turned persistently weak.
